risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The forward-looking statement names economic conditions affecting demand/supply and price conditions as an important factor that could impact the Company's performance.
- The cautionary statement lists changes in Government policies, regulations, tax laws, other statutes and incidental factors among the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.
- The Company states it operates one plant, at Tarapur, Maharashtra, with the head office in Masjid, Mumbai, so operations depend on a single manufacturing location.
- The MD&A states primary liquidity needs are to finance working capital, funded by internal accruals and borrowings, and explains the Debt-Equity Ratio rose from 0.25 to 0.33 'due to higher borrowings during the year', with Debt Service Coverage Ratio down 9.78%.
- The ratio disclosure shows Net profit ratio at 0.84%, Return on Capital employed down 16.31% and Return on equity down 9.23% year on year, leaving little cushion against cost or price shocks.
- The secretarial auditor's observations record non-disclosure of the 50,00,000 warrants allotted on 23rd May 2025 in the shareholding pattern filed with the exchange, non-disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulation 29(2) and PIT Regulation 7(2) for 7.09% shares sold by Suraj Tradelinks (Promoter Body Corporate), no filing of the statement of deviation/variation of preferential warrant proceeds, and dissatisfaction with the completeness of the structured digital database.
- Annexure B discloses total foreign exchange used of Rs 1108.20 Lakh against foreign exchange earned (FOB) of Rs 298.23 Lakh, leaving the Company a net user of foreign currency and exposed to currency movement.
- Annexure B shows electricity, coal, diesel and biomass briquette consumption for the plant, with coal quantity rising from 281.441 tons to 1,724.694 tons, making fuel price and availability a structural cost factor; the Board states only that energy-conservation measures such as monitoring power consumption and installing a Dual Fuel Burner were taken.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Increase capacity across all products in line with product demand.
- Pursue backward and forward integration into products such as DMA-HCL and Ortho chloro benzoic acid, and into further APIs such as theophylline; management states necessary steps have been initiated.
- Retain earnings rather than pay a dividend because the company is going for expansion.
